turns.prompt:
You are given alloy_pair_max_train.csv, a steel/superalloy dataset of 300 samples. Each sample is described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), and the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).

Build a predictive model, then propose the COMPLETE recipe (composition + processing + categoricals) that MAXIMIZES yield strength.

Validity is required: every wt% ≥ 0 and the alloying elements must sum to ≤ 100 (Fe is the balance) — an invalid recipe scores zero.

State the predicted yield strength in MPa, then end your answer with the
complete recipe as a single `Final:` block — comma-separated `name=value`
pairs, exactly these field names, no blank line inside it (Fe is the balance,
do not state it):

Final: C=<wt%>, Mn=<wt%>, Si=<wt%>, Cr=<wt%>, Ni=<wt%>, Mo=<wt%>, V=<wt%>,
Nb=<wt%>, Co=<wt%>, Al=<wt%>, Ti=<wt%>, Cu=<wt%>, solutionizing_temp=<°C>,
aging_temp=<°C>, aging_time=<h>, cooling_rate=<K/s>,
heat_treatment=<annealed|quenched|quench_temper|solution_aged>, route=<cast|wrought|AM>
turns.answer_text:
**Predicted yield strength: 712.93 MPa.**

I used a non-extrapolating **1-nearest-neighbor regression model**, with range-scaled numerical features and categorical mismatch indicators. Fe was excluded as an independent feature because it is determined by the composition.

The recipe below maximizes this model’s prediction and corresponds to the strongest measured sample. Its alloying elements total **33.5401 wt%**, satisfying the nonnegativity and composition-sum constraints. This is a training-supported candidate, not an independently validated physical optimum.
